title: Late-binding weight compression format mismatch — stability & accuracy regression action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A model onboarding change introduced a late-binding weight compression format variant that omitted a per-tensor scale metadata field. Dequantization for affected tensors produced small systematic offsets which, when combined with continuous batching and the kernel-fallback path triggered under load, produced correctness drift in generation (measurable accuracy regression) and a crash loop for certain large-context requests. This ticket tracks immediate mitigations, root-cause remediation, and follow-up preventative controls.
detection: Automated regression alerts from the evaluation pipeline flagged a 0.6% drop in Rouge-L on our standardized prompt set at 2026-03-09 21:17 UTC. Simultaneously the serving alerting channel reported an uptick in OOM/retry loops on hosts using the fallback mixed-kernel path. On-call correlated logs and model hashes to a recent model upload that used the new weight-compression pipeline promoted the night before.
impact:
- Production traffic: ~2.4% of hosted requests routed to the affected model family experienced degraded output quality; latency for affected requests increased by ~30% due to retrying on fallback kernels.
- Customer reports: 3 customers opened tickets describing hallucination/regression symptoms; one customer temporarily disabled auto-updates.
- Revenue/SLAs: No SLA breach, but measurable UX regression and internal dashboards show increased error budget consumption on the model route.

root_cause: The model-onboarding pipeline introduced a late-binding compressed-weight format that allowed omission of an optional per-tensor quant-scale metadata field for backward compatibility. The runtime's dequantizer assumed the presence of that scale and applied a default scale of 1.0 silently, producing small but systematic value offsets. Under normal kernels this produced a small accuracy drift; under certain sequence lengths the kernel selector fell back to a mixed-precision compatibility path which had a different expectation for tensor layout, triggering an index-safety check failure and causing repeated request retries and crash loops.
mitigations_done: Hotfix: model-loader now rejects compressed weight blobs that do not include the required quant-scale header (deployed 2026-03-09 23:05 UTC)
Rollback: Canary promoted model rolled back to previous artifact across regions (completed 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC)
Canary throttling: temporarily disabled auto-promotion of model packages until validation gates are added
Customer communication: triage notes and recommended temporary workaround (pin model version) sent to affected customers
long_term_actions: Add strict format contract and end-to-end checksum: enforce magic bytes + schema validation in onboarding pipeline (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 3)
Expand model-onboarding unit tests: include randomized compressed-weight permutations, intentionally malformed header cases, and round-trip dequant checks (owner: Lina Zhao, estimate: 5)
Kernel selector improvement: make fallback path tolerant to legacy-layout tensors by adding a compatibility shim and explicit op-fingerprint checks (owner: Rafael Gomez, estimate: 8)
Improve canary gates: require internal eval delta < 0.2% on our prompt-suite before any auto-promotion; add manual review for format changes (owner: PM - Serena Lim, estimate: 2)
Observability: add per-request dequant delta histogram and op-layout mismatch counter to runtime telemetry and set alerts (owner: Observability team - Priya Kulkarni, estimate: 3)

Backward-compat migration plan: provide a deterministic migration tool that converts old compressed artifacts to the new schema and flags incompatible models (owner: ModelOps - Diego Fernandes, estimate: 4)

postmortem_notes: Key lesson: format compatibility trade-offs must be guarded by explicit schema validation and strong canary gating. The combination of a minor per-tensor metadata omission plus an orthogonal kernel fallback path produced a compound failure mode that individual subsystems' unit-tests did not catch. We will adopt a policy: any change to on-disk/model-artifact schema must have a migration plan, a backward-compatibility test suite, and a human review before canary promotion.
